kpi.price.label: Price
kpi.price.desc: Latest traded price per share, in the listing currency.
kpi.market_cap.label: Market cap
kpi.market_cap.desc: Share price × shares outstanding — what the market says the equity is worth.
kpi.ev.label: Enterprise value
kpi.ev.desc: Market cap plus debt minus cash — the price of the whole business, not just the equity.
kpi.ev.note: cap + net debt; check debt against latest 10-Q on EDGAR
kpi.pe_ttm.label: P/E (TTM)
kpi.pe_ttm.desc: Price / earnings per share over the trailing twelve months. Lower = cheaper per unit of current profit.
kpi.pe_fwd.label: P/E (fwd)
kpi.pe_fwd.desc: Price / next-year consensus EPS. Below the TTM P/E means analysts expect earnings to grow.
kpi.peg.label: PEG (TTM)
kpi.peg.desc: P/E divided by expected EPS growth — a growth-adjusted P/E. Under ~1 is classically 'cheap for its growth'.
kpi.peg.note: yfinance PEG is unreliable — never act on it without cross-check
kpi.pb.label: P/B
kpi.pb.desc: Price / book (accounting) value per share. Most meaningful for banks and asset-heavy businesses.
kpi.ev_ebitda.label: EV/EBITDA
kpi.ev_ebitda.desc: Enterprise value / earnings before interest, tax, depreciation & amortisation — a P/E that ignores capital structure, comparable across leverage.
kpi.ev_sales.label: EV/Sales
kpi.ev_sales.desc: Enterprise value / revenue. The fallback multiple for high-growth or not-yet-profitable names where P/E breaks down.
kpi.roe.label: ROE
kpi.roe.desc: Return on equity: net income / shareholder equity. Profitability of the equity base — note leverage inflates it.
kpi.roic.label: ROIC
kpi.roic.desc: Return on invested capital: after-tax operating profit / all capital employed (equity + debt). How well the whole business compounds; >15% sustained is a quality mark.
kpi.gross_margin.label: Gross margin
kpi.gross_margin.desc: Revenue minus cost of goods sold, as % of revenue — pricing power on the product itself.
kpi.op_margin.label: Operating margin
kpi.op_margin.desc: Operating profit as % of revenue — what the core business keeps after operating costs.
kpi.net_margin.label: Net margin
kpi.net_margin.desc: Net income as % of revenue — the bottom line after interest and tax.
kpi.fcf.label: FCF (last FY)
kpi.fcf.desc: Free cash flow: operating cash flow minus capital expenditure — the cash left over to pay dividends, buy back shares or reinvest.
kpi.fcf_yield.label: FCF yield
kpi.fcf_yield.desc: Free cash flow / market cap — the cash return you buy at today's price (the inverse of the FCF multiple).
kpi.net_debt_ebitda.label: Net debt / EBITDA
kpi.net_debt_ebitda.desc: Debt minus cash, divided by EBITDA — roughly the years of operating profit needed to repay the debt. <1 conservative, >3 heavy; negative = more cash than debt.
kpi.cash_conversion.label: Cash conversion (FCF/NI)
kpi.cash_conversion.desc: Free cash flow / net income — how much of accounting profit turns into actual cash.
kpi.cash_conversion.note: >1 sustained is a quality signal; <1 check accruals
kpi.revenue_cagr.label: Revenue CAGR (5y stmts)
kpi.revenue_cagr.desc: Compound annual growth rate of revenue over the last ~5 fiscal years of filed statements.
kpi.net_income_cagr.label: Net income CAGR (5y stmts)
kpi.net_income_cagr.desc: Compound annual growth rate of net income over the last ~5 fiscal years.
kpi.fcf_cagr.label: FCF CAGR (5y stmts)
kpi.fcf_cagr.desc: Compound annual growth rate of free cash flow over the last ~5 fiscal years.
kpi.share_dilution.label: Diluted shares CAGR
kpi.share_dilution.desc: Yearly change in diluted share count. Positive = you're being diluted (usually stock comp); negative = net buybacks shrinking the share count.
kpi.moat.label: Moat score
kpi.moat.desc: 0-100 heuristic of how much moat *evidence* the filings show: persistent ROIC (30%), stable gross margins (25%), durable growth (15%), cash conversion (15%), share-count discipline (15%). ≥70 wide, 45-70 narrow, <45 no moat. A screen, not a verdict.
kpi.moat.note: quant proxies only — cannot see brand, network effects or switching costs
